title: Editing in the viewer
body: Dragging an object in acre-gui rewrites the number in the source that placed it. Every value keeps its span, so an edit replaces the text under one span and needs no new parser. The first version covers static figures: literal `at X Y`, the offsets of `at NAME DX DY`, `points` pairs and literal `from`/`to` ends, with an `at` inserted where a node has none. It refuses a value from a `let`, a `( ... )` expression or a `style`, a child a stack or grid places, a repeat copy, and an object a timeline moves, with the reason in the status line. With the neovim link the viewer sends an edit message that the plugin applies when the buffer has not changed since; without it the viewer writes the file. A drag on an object moves it and a drag on empty canvas pans. No new key bindings.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/0c799e42
notes.text:
Dragging an object to move it works as of aa7933d, and acre-cfb6e6 is closed. Still to do for this milestone:

- resize handles that stretch a shape's `size`
- dragging a vertex of `points`
- dragging one end of a connector
- reordering the children of a stack by dragging
- the hand checks in acre-66ca87, which now include a drag in the real viewer with and without the neovim link
